items.title: A two-periodic complex formed from two injective endomorphisms with commuting images over a one dimensional Noetherian local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite module M of dimension one over a Noetherian local ring A and two injective endomorphisms phi, psi with phi(psi(M)) = psi(phi(M)) - for instance commuting endomorphisms - the lemma asserts that M/phi psi M has finite length and that (M/phi psi M, phi, psi) is an exact (2, 1)-periodic complex (statement lines 17370-17380). The proof localises at a minimal prime q of the support of M, where M_q has finite length and both endomorphisms consequently become isomorphisms, so the support of M/phi psi M is concentrated at the closed point and hence has finite length (proof lines 17383-17389). Exactness is then checked directly: the kernel of phi on M/phi psi M is visibly psi M/phi psi M, so the kernel of phi is the image of psi, and the symmetric statement follows from the hypothesis M/phi psi M = M/psi phi M (proof lines 17390-17394). Recognising that injectivity plus the commuting-image condition is exactly what makes the two kernel computations match is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
